svg.title: Execution lanes
svg.desc: A request enters one of two lanes. The primary lane has one permit outside pool_size; the worker lane has providers.<id>.pool_size permits per provider. After a permit the coordinator hands out the primary runner, a cached worker or a new one as an ExecutionLease, released exactly once to the cache, to disposal, or to quarantine when termination is unconfirmed.

g.text: Hover a box for its rule and the code that decides it; its connections light up. Click a box to open its section.
Inside a rendered document this image is static. Click it to open the interactive SVG.

svg.text: Capacity is permits, not processes: pool_size caps concurrent executions per provider and idle cached workers hold none.

g.text: Interactive, channel turns · channel turns take the primary lane; interactive ones only when provider and policy match the primary runner's
Lane choice is ExecutionCoordinator._laneFor. Admission is wait: the request queues for a permit.
Cron, temporary conversations · scheduler and temporary surfaces always run on the worker lane and wait for a permit
A temporary session reuses its retained worker and the permit that worker kept while cached.
Tasks, workflow steps · acquire returns null or BusyTurnException when no permit is free; TaskExecutor retries on its next poll
A polled task or workflow request takes its permit before global admission, so a refused attempt leaves no loop or rate state.
Primary gate · one permit for the deployment's primary runner: main-agent turns are serialized
WorkerCapacityGate(1) in ExecutionCoordinator; unaffected by providers.<id>.pool_size or container count.
wait for a permit, or fail fast
Worker gate, one per provider · a ceiling on concurrent executions, not a process count: idle cached harnesses hold no permit
A provider with no gate is a StateError. A quarantined permit lowers effective capacity (ADR-058).
Primary TurnRunner · no worker is created: the lease carries the primary runner
Releasing the lease returns the permit and leaves the runner alone.
Cached worker · _takeCached: a healthy exact-session worker, else a healthy host worker with the same provider, policy, agent, workspace
Container workers also need the exact logical-agent principal. Requests with execution-scoped inputs skip the cache.
must come up idle; single-use if scoped
New worker · createWorker builds the runner, harness.start() runs, and a runner whose provider or policy mismatches the request is discarded
Before creating, _scavenge drops the oldest idle cached workers beyond the effective capacity left.
idempotent: released exactly once on success, failure, cancel or setup error; the active set drives busy/free observability
ExecutionLease · the caller's handle to one runner; release() is memoized, so every path may call it
Teardown order: harness termination, authority revocation, container destruction. Capacity returns only after it completes.
Back to cache · a temporary-session worker keeps its permit while cached; other cached workers hold none
Task and workflow containers never qualify, and neither do single-use workers.
Dispose · everything else: single-use workers, task and workflow containers, a runner that is not reusable or not idle
The permit returns once teardown is confirmed.
Quarantine the permit · root-process exit, container revocation or container destruction could not be confirmed
The slot stays withheld so a fresh authority is never admitted over a live orphan (ADR-058).
